objective: Proof and computation. A group's coset law composes like cycles exactly when every subgroup has a unique maximal normal subgroup; such groups have all Sylow subgroups cyclic and an abelian top G/N of prime order. Every knot of such a law is pulled back from a cyclic p-group knot, so every system reduces to a linear system over Z_(q^K), and by RIGID-SELECTION D the top image after any removal from a global failure on a substrate is at most one line. The law is rigid when the order is squarefree; D9 and F20 keep knots below the top through cyclic sections of order 9 and 4. Checked on every such group up to order 60, with brute force on small substrates for those up to order 24.
status: Proved by TOP-LAYER-20261102-001B-P001: a group's coset law composes like cycles iff every subgroup has a unique maximal normal subgroup; such groups have cyclic Sylows, prime top G/N and cyclic p-group abelianizations (18 non-abelian ones up to order 60); knots are pulled back from cyclic p-group relations, systems reduce to square Z_(p^K) systems, and by RIGID-SELECTION D the top image after any removal from a global failure is at most one line. Rigid for squarefree order; C5:C4 and D9 keep knots below the top
title: Group laws keep their top rigid
